## One bracket, unknowns on both sides {#one-bracket}

Expand the bracket first. Keep the equation balanced as you gather the unknown terms and isolate $x$.

:::::: {.example-pair}
::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$4(x+3)=2x+18$

::: {.fragment}

[Expand the bracket.]{.annotation}

$4x+12=2x+18$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Subtract $2x$ from both sides.]{.annotation}

$2x+12=18$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Subtract $12$ from both sides.]{.annotation}

$2x=6$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Divide both sides by $2$.]{.annotation}

$\dfrac{2x}{2}=\dfrac{6}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=3$

:::
:::::
::::: {.paper}
::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$4(x-3)=2x+18$

Only the sign inside the bracket changes. What changes after expansion? Solve on paper.

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$\begin{aligned}
4x-12&=2x+18\\
2x-12&=18\\
2x&=30\\
\dfrac{2x}{2}&=\dfrac{30}{2}\\
x&=15
\end{aligned}$

The constant is now $-12$, so add $12$ to both sides.

:::
